clue.text: Type of verb I've not used — but getting there

indicators.note: something not used is left out, so these letters are dropped from the verb type

parts.note: an intransitive verb is one that takes no direct object
taken as its three letters

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on a verb that is skipped, while someone is still on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods or travellers on the journey, not yet arrived, are said to be in transit.

clue.text: Across the pond, holding court's first part of hearing

indicators.note: holding means having inside, so the court's opening letter goes within

parts.note: for a Briton, across the Atlantic means in the US

indicators.note: the first letter of the court word

explanation.surface: In America, an opening session of a court case is the first hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like a court session, but it means the sense of hearing: the incus is a bone of the middle ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The anvil-shaped small bone in the middle ear transmits vibration, so it is part of the hearing organ.

clue.text: Canvas where, by curious art, Linus shortly appeared

indicators.note: curious means odd, so these three letters are reordered
shortly means cut short, so the last letter of the surname is dropped

parts.note: Linus Pauling was the American chemist who won two Nobel prizes

explanation.surface: A painting scene where a man named Linus briefly showed up among odd art.
explanation.walkthrough: Linus stands for the chemist's surname, Pauling, which loses its G.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a heavy waterproof sheet of canvas used as a cover.

clue.text: Titled Russian wasting year in a horrible part of the world

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so the letter for year is taken away

parts.note: nasty means horrible
Asia is a continent, a part of the world

explanation.surface: A Russian aristocrat squanders a year in a dreadful region.
explanation.walkthrough: Grand Duchess Anastasia was the youngest daughter of the last Tsar.
explanation.definitionFit: Anastasia Romanov was a grand duchess, a member of the Russian royal family with a title.

clue.text: One that's retiring in silk overnight for a change

indicators.note: change signals that these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone going to bed in silk night clothes for once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like going to bed, which the silk surface supports; it means shy.
explanation.definitionFit: A very shy person who avoids attention is called this, after the modest woodland flower.

clue.text: Be late in expressing revolutionary disapproval

definitions.text: Be late in expressing revolutionary disapproval

parts.words: Be late in expressing revolutionary disapproval
parts.note: the late are the dead, and a dead person said to rotate in the tomb shows disapproval by revolving

explanation.surface: A slow protester voices objections to a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means dead and 'revolutionary' means spinning round, not political.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says a dead person would be appalled by something, as though spinning in the tomb.

clue.text: Good tool to take in hand

parts.note: a rasp is a coarse file used by woodworkers

explanation.surface: Advice that a decent implement should be held in the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To grip something firmly in the hand is to seize hold of it, a synonym.

clue.text: Study costume

definitions.meaning: to work up a subject, mastering it for an exam

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to learn up a topic, and the noun means an outfit or costume.

clue.text: Article about my fruit

indicators.note: about means around, so the article wraps the exclamation

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!

explanation.surface: A piece of writing on one's own fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is an exclamation, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The nut of the oak tree is botanically its fruit.

clue.text: Express strong feeling about son taking on job

indicators.note: taking on means joining up, so the feeling follows the job

parts.note: a post is a job

indicators.note: about means around, so the feeling wraps the letter for son

parts.note: hate is a strong feeling

explanation.surface: Someone expresses fierce feelings about a son getting a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like a verb, but it is the adverb meaning with great speed.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something with all possible speed is to do it at express speed.

clue.text: Main villain right to appeal, to be strangled by rope potentially

indicators.note: being strangled means having something wrapped tightly round, so these letters go inside the fibre

parts.note: coir is coconut fibre that can be made into rope
SA is short for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A villain on the high seas claims a right of appeal before being hanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, so a main villain is a pirate of the high seas.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a pirate, a robber on the sea, which old writing calls the main.

clue.text: Ignoring starter, addresses the food

indicators.note: ignoring the starter means the first letter of the speeches is left off

parts.note: formal speeches are addresses or orations

explanation.surface: Someone skips the first course and gives speeches about the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a first course of the food, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rations are fixed allowances of provisions, so the supplies of food for troops or travellers.

clue.text: It's not stupid to feel hurt

definitions.meaning: to sting, as a cut or a slight does

explanation.surface: A claim that feeling pain is no sign of foolishness.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means clever and intelligent; the verb means to sting with pain.

clue.text: Brad's driver has nothing to hold a hot drink

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so the letter sits within the zero

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero
punch is a drink often served hot, of spirits and spice

explanation.surface: A man named Brad, chauffeur, has no money to buy a warming drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Brad looks like a man's name; a brad is a small thin nail, and a nail punch drives it in.
explanation.definitionFit: A brad is a slender nail, and the tool used to sink nails below the surface drives it.

clue.text: Cover dale together, a long way

definitions.meaning: joined up the words make Coverdale: Myles or ... Coverdale translated the first complete printed English Bible
a great distance, many units of 1760 yards

explanation.surface: Someone tells a walker to cross the valley in company, a fair distance.
explanation.walkthrough: Run 'Cover dale' together and it is the surname of the Tudor Bible translator, whose first name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Units of distance in plural stand for a great distance, as in miles away; Coverdale's Christian name was the same word.

clue.text: Rural accent of actor, where he's filming

parts.note: a mummer is an actor in a traditional folk play
a film set is where the filming happens

explanation.surface: An actor's country voice, used on location.
explanation.walkthrough: Mummerset is the vague West Country accent stage actors put on for yokels.
explanation.definitionFit: An invented stage dialect of rustic English, made up by actors to sound countrified.

clue.text: Reagan announcing his displeasure with foreign decoration

parts.note: Ronald Reagan introducing himself would say I, Ron
to be cross is to show displeasure

explanation.surface: An American president voices his anger about a medal from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Picture Reagan declaring 'I, Ron, (am) cross'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Cross is a German military medal, so a decoration from another country.

clue.text: Our time has no peer — ace!

parts.note: in Britain a commoner is anyone who is not a peer, a titled noble
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A boast that our age is unequalled and first rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no peer' looks like praise but means not a noble.
explanation.definitionFit: The period counted from the birth of Christ, used in dates, is the present era.

clue.text: Do another trip in car

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so these letters tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A suggestion to take another journey by car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a journey, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling by motor along a highway, someone driving is said to be on the move by car.

clue.text: He produced essays, meaning to broadcast

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters seed widely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An essayist whose meaning is meant to be spread far and wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to broadcast' looks like a single verb, but 'to' is fodder and 'broadcast' alone scatters the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Michel de Montaigne, the French Renaissance writer, invented the essay as a literary form.

clue.text: Power, say, to capture rook for bishop — one's ahead

indicators.note: capturing something means taking it in, so the chess piece letter goes inside
say signals that the word for power is heard, not read

parts.note: might means power or strength
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A chess move where power lets a rook be taken in exchange for a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: the bishop wears it, and 'one's ahead' reads as 'one's a head(dress)'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's tall pointed ceremonial hat, worn on the head, is the headgear meant.

clue.text: Man of the world first to look into reducing shocking risks

indicators.note: into places the single letter inside the electrical word

parts.note: earthing an appliance connects it to the ground so that it cannot give electric shocks

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word is all that is taken

explanation.surface: A worldly man begins to look at ways of cutting dangers that would shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' looks like an anagram signal, but the phrase describes electrical earthing, a British term for grounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction calls a human from planet Earth by this name, a man of this world.

clue.text: Hood for one that's not finished dressing

indicators.note: the word is not finished, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: robing is putting on robes, dressing

explanation.surface: A hooded garment that is only half dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' looks like a garment; it is Robin Hood, the outlaw of Sherwood.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin is the first name of the legendary English outlaw Hood, an example.

clue.text: Physicist is fine in garden

indicators.note: in places the word for fine inside the gardening word

parts.note: to hoe is to work a garden with a hoe
OK means fine

explanation.surface: A scientist relaxes happily among the flower beds.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Hooke was a seventeenth-century English scientist, known for his law of elasticity.

clue.text: Follows governor in larger than usual case

indicators.note: in places the governor inside the size abbreviation

parts.note: OS is outsize, a clothing or luggage size larger than normal
a bey was a governor of an Ottoman province

explanation.surface: A provincial ruler packs an oversized suitcase and goes along with orders.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply with commands or rules is to do as they say, to follow them.

clue.text: Country lawyer submerged in paper

indicators.note: submerged means sunk inside, so the lawyer goes within the newspaper

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
DA is a district attorney, a US prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A rural lawyer buried in paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country lawyer' reads as one phrase; 'Country' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan is a nation in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Boats need fuel — it's under the bed

parts.note: subs are submarines, which sailors call boats
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Vessels must refuel, and the store is kept below the bunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a garden bed or the topsoil, not the one slept in.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsoil is the layer of earth lying beneath the topsoil, below a flower bed.

clue.text: Done curiously with air, not with liquid

indicators.note: done curiously means done in an odd way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something is accomplished oddly using air rather than any liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just links the two lots of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An aneroid barometer measures pressure with a sealed box instead of mercury or other fluid.

clue.text: A column of numbers -— nine, finally —- is drawn

parts.note: in written sums the tens column holds the second digits

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the number word

explanation.surface: An accountant adds up a column of figures, nine at the bottom, with a ruled line.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn tight like a rope, a stretched or taut thing is said to be under strain.

clue.text: Time to cut down forest for book

parts.note: to hew is to chop down trees
the Forest of Arden is the English woodland of As You Like It

explanation.surface: A call to start felling trees, for paper to make books.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope's novel, first of the Barchester series, carries this title.
